newsitem.title: UK: Buoyant dollar bounds to fresh highs in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant dollar bounds to fresh highs in Europe.

text.p: The high-flying dollar soared to its best levels in years in European morning trade, with analysts saying promising economic fundamentals all around are set to push it further on its bullish way.

The dollar kept firmly above the key level of 1.6400 marks and just below 119 yen by the European midsession, although the market cooled off slightly from earlier levels as it shook off some sellers after its breathtaking surge.

"There's a huge appetite for the dollar/mark out there. German exporters are selling into the dollar rally, but the demand is so huge, the market is just soaking it all up," said a trader at a British bank.
The dollar was at 1.6413/18 marks at 1205 GMT, off its high of 1.6455 marks, its best level since June 1994, but still way above its late Tuesday level of 1.6242/52.

It strengthened this morning on a combination of pro-dollar economic fundamentals and relief that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in a speech on Tuesday made no comments that might damage the dollar.
"Everyone was worried yesterday that Greenspan would say something that would hurt the dollar. But he didn't, so now all the people who were waiting are in the market this morning," the trader said.

In his testimony to the U.S. Senate budget committee, Greenspan gave an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy. He said U.S. labour markets were "exceptionally tight" but added that this has not led to accelerated wages or inflation.
However, Greenspan tempered his upbeat assessment by warning that the surprising lack of inflation pressures could not last forever and the Fed needed to be wary.
"The comments from Greenspan and other Fed officials overnight tended to be on the hawkish side," said PaineWebber international economist James McKay.

"And although we don't expect a U.S. rate hike anytime soon, the market is really starting to confirm that Fed policy is now looking towards higher interest rates in the next couple of months," McKay said.

The dollar also got ammunition from a host of factors away from home -- an Italian rate cut, German data showing a muted business climate, concerns over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health, and the Bank of France governor's reported comment that the dollar's strength matched the wishes of the G7.

"It's all coming together -- people have set in their minds clear targets of the mid 1.60s against the mark...and 120 to 125 against the yen," said Stephen Hannah, director of research at IBJ International in London.
The dollar was standing at 118.90/00 yen at 1158 GMT, softening from its 47-month high of 119.20 hit earlier but more than one yen above late Tuesday levels of 117.82/87.
The level of 120 yen, a big barrier both technically and psychologically, was now looking very much within reach although it will be tough to break, traders said.
On the way to that level, the dollar will find resistance at 119.45/50, said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.

The dollar's strength across the board also took it to a 32-month high against the Swiss franc. Dollar/Swiss was at 1.4315/25 at 1203 GMT, surging from its late Tuesday level of 1.4150/70 although off its high of 1.4360. +44-171-542-6721
